newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli shares end lower after Wall Street fall.
newsitem.headline: Israeli shares end lower after Wall Street fall.

text.p: Israeli shares closed broadly lower in thin trading on Sunday in response to the decline on Wall Street on Friday and an expectedly high June consumer price index, traders said.

The benchmark Mishtanim index of the top 100 shares fell 1.17 percent, or 3.50 points, to 294.62 on a low all-share turnover of 115 million shekels against 181 million shekels on Thursday, the last day of trading before the Israeli weekend.
The Maof 25 blue chip index closed 1.17 percent lower at 301.15.

"Trading was very dull today and the market fell on relatively low volume. It's partly because of the Dow's decline on Friday and partly because many investors are on summer vacation and there is no one to buy," said Ron Weisberg at IBI Investment House.
The Dow Jones Industrial Average dropped 130 points on Friday.
"The market suffered from the 'Wall Street effect' today but the negative trend started last Wednesday following the higher-than-expected CPI," said Eli Nahum, head of trading at Zannex Securities.
The June consumer price index, released last Tuesday, rose 1.1 percent, well above expectations, and has heightened fears of an interest rate rise later this month.
"Despite that, there are very few sellers. It seems that buyers are waiting for the market to fall a little more before they step in," Nahum said.
"At the current level the market lacks strength to go on rising," he added.

Weisberg said investors were also waiting for the market to calm down after the expiry of the Maof June contracts this Thursday. Analysts said the market feared options players might dump shares on the market in the run-up in order to lower the index.

The most active shares were Koor Industries, which rose 2.75 percent to 36,843 agorot on volume of 14.1 million shekels; Bezeq Israel Telecom, which fell 3.0 percent to 1,026 agorot on volume of 7.5 million shekels; and Delek the Israel Fuel Corp, which dropped 2.75 percent to 10,936 agorot on turnover of 4.3 million shekels.
It was the second session of sharp drops for Delek, which has fallen on news that its Delek Automotive Systems DLAE.TA subsidiary is being charged with tax evasion to the tune of 100 million shekels.
Trading in Delek Automotive was suspended on Sunday.
- Dan Gerstenfeld, Tel Aviv newsroom, 972-3-537-2211 x233
